title: LA-MTL: Latency-Aware Automated Multi-Task Learning
problem: Multi-task learning on embedded devices must simultaneously optimize task accuracy, parameter efficiency, and inference latency, but existing MTL approaches lack explicit latency constraints in the search, often requiring post-hoc tuning that compromises accuracy or efficiency.
motivation: Real-time multi-workload embedded applications (e.g., Jetson AGX Orin) require tight latency bounds; naive MTL parameter reduction sacrifices latency guarantees or task metrics.
method: LA-MTL performs layer-level automated MTL policy search incorporating a novel Analytical Latency Factor (ALF) that captures local and global latencies during search. The framework derives Pareto-optimal solutions balancing task metrics, parameter efficiency, and latency constraints via architecture search on shared backbone layers.
key_novelty: Analytical Latency Factor (ALF) enabling direct latency awareness during MTL policy search without post-hoc optimization or Pareto iteration.
contributions: Layer-level MTL policy search with latency constraints
Analytical Latency Factor (ALF) capturing local and global inference latency
50% latency reduction on Jetson AGX Orin while maintaining ±2 p.p. accuracy on semantic segmentation and depth estimation
20+ p.p. parameter efficiency improvement over state-of-the-art MTL

metrics.other: 20+ p.p. parameter efficiency gain; ±2 p.p. accuracy on CityScapes

limitations: Evaluation on two vision tasks (segmentation, depth); transferability to other domains (NLP, speech) and heterogeneous hardware not discussed.
primary_theme: latency-aware multi-task learning via analytical latency-driven search
